findings.reason: §2 should have said it extends `insert_section` in reckon/_store.py, not that it adds a parallel target, which is what the subsequent repair nodes were forced to reconcile.
findings.text: §2 introduces `append target 'sections'` (now mcp.py:1704) as a new create/attach interface while the design text is silent on the pre-existing `insert_section` op (mcp.py:1712, reckon/_store.py:3110 `_apply_insert_section`), so the same section-creation behaviour is reached by two state routes and the plan gives no justification for a second route over extending the first — the landed history bears the cost out, since two later repair nodes (`e4be85c9`, `98c976c5`) were spent converging the two routes' validation and repairing cases that pinned the older op

findings.reason: the plan should name the declaration map as the owner and have the record's status derive from it (or state why the two must be stored separately), instead of adding a second store for one fact.
findings.text: §1 makes each section record carry `status` (SectionRecord.status, reckon/_schema.py:948, enum `SECTION_DECLARATION_ENUM`) mirroring the existing `plan-section-declarations` map, so a section's declared state now has two authoritative homes, and the design does not say which wins or that one is derived from the other — the landed §8/§9 follow-ons already had to make `derive_impl_from_sections` take the declarations as a second input to bridge the two

findings.reason: each added section must, in its own text, either retire/merge the pre-existing route and finding it duplicates (e.g. the untyped `insert_section`) or state why the surface cannot be avoided.
findings.text: §1/§2 add public surface — the `SectionRecord` definition to the published schema (docs/_shared/plan.schema.json:459, +1 public definition), the `append target 'sections'` and the newly required `effort_hours`/`capability`/`links` fields on `insert_section` to the MCP op vocabulary (mcp.py:1704, :1712), and §2/§6/§7 add refusal/finding families (`section-record-invalid`, `unwired-plan`, `plan-ref-could-be-section-ref`) — and none of these sections name what they retire or merge, or state why nothing can be, so the added surface (mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23) is unaccounted for in the section text

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design lands behind existing owners rather than a new module family: the record is one `SectionRecord` in reckon/_schema.py:919, impl is one `derive_impl_from_sections` (reckon/_plan_html.py:318), and §7's wiring rule is one `unwired_plan_finding` (reckon/doccheck.py:863) called by the audit, the create boundary and the roadmap rather than spelled three times.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §1's section record carries a `status` field that mirrors the `plan-section-declarations` map, so the same fact has two homes; the owner to extend is the declaration parser in reckon/_plan_html.py.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §1/§2/§5/§7 add to the MCP op vocabulary and to the refusal/audit finding families without any section naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the two codebases it names and cites the mechanisms it extends: `parse_plan_ref` (reckon/_schema.py:274), `depends_on`/`gated_sections` resolution, the `plan-section-declarations` map (reckon/_plan_html.py:530), and `CapabilityRequest` (reckon/_schema.py:891), with a recorded S22 reuse map over 14 sections and 55 verified citations; the landed `SectionRecord` reuses `CapabilityRequest` verbatim rather than authoring a parallel capability type.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §2 adds an `append` target `sections` as a second section-creation route beside the pre-existing `insert_section` state op, and its design text never names `insert_section` nor says why that op cannot be extended, leaving two live routes into the same machinery.
